answer: An agent economy can map trust as a living graph: each attestation is an edge, and trust flows outward from long-standing agents, thinning with every hop until it reaches its nadir at the fringe. A Sybil farm spins a dense knot of self-attestations, but the knot hangs hollow — no edges reach the trusted core, so its flow reads near zero. Every identity must earn its own onyx edge back to the core through real, unrelated sponsors, and each new fake dilutes the farm's flow further, so the fiftieth fake costs far more attestation-work than the first.
